utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, our next witness is Mr. Vojnovic, Milos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before I start I have to inform Your Honours that this witness has poor eyesight due to diabetes and we had to re-arrange his testimony completely because he couldn't follow the documents and we changed a lot of -- we made a lot of changes. So he has a statement and I think that we owe Your Honours and the Prosecutor some corrections, and we received an e-mail from Prosecutor, they complained about paragraphs 27, 28, and 29 from his statement. Paragraph 27 they are right, it cannot be Exhibit Number 6D614, but rather 6D787. In paragraph 28, the page was wrong, it's 648 instead of 647, point is correct. Paragraph 29, this exhibit just has to be removed, we don't have exhibit on this issue. We also found another mistake in paragraph 33, this exhibit has to be removed as well, it doesn't respond to this paragraph, it's 6D604. We couldn't find proof for paragraph 48, so we would kindly ask Your Honours to allow us to remove this paragraph from the statement of this witness. And we -- there is a mistake in paragraph 52, the last one. This was discovered by the witness. He warned me that the last sentence should be: "When the war started these departments virtually ceased to exist because the members of the RPO, reserve police departments, were VJ and police," should be added, "reservists who were mobilised and attached to military units and engaged as police reservists after declaration of a state of war." And that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you should now start the examination and we'll deal with these once you've presented the exhibit. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Two things, Your Honour. One of them relates to paragraph 28 where I understood Mr. Lukic to say that the reference should be to 6D614, page 648.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But I could use some assistance on where that is in the English translation. In e-court the English document is only 500 and some pages and I don't know where to find page 648, item 366.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have it in English yet. I think we are close to this page with the translation, but it's not uploaded yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So not available yet, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the second one is, Your Honour, in paragraph 27 I was told that reference to 6D614 should be changed to 6D787, but I don't believe 6D787 was on the notification for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No doubt that's because it was 6D614. You're going to cope with that one, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's get started, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vojnovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you could hear, we had some corrections in relation to your statement. I will now commence the part of your testimony that is live, and then we will go back to your statement which is Exhibit 6D1532.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, I need one instruction from Your Honours. Should I ask the witness now about if he's accepting this corrected statement or to deal with it afterwards?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you should ask him the usual questions you ask about the statement and ask him if he heard the alterations being made and whether these are appropriate, and then invite us to admit the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, we will, therefore, go back to your statement. As you have heard, you and I discussed these amendments this morning, especially the last paragraph, about the reservists. If you were to testify today on this topic, would you provide the same statement as the one that is provided here to the Court with all its amendments?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have it before me. Can I take it out of my bag?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please let me know which page I should look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First page 7, paragraph 27, all we changed here is the number of the exhibit. These numbers mean nothing to you. There was a mistake and we changed the number of the exhibit. It's not 6D614, rather, 6D787. The only alteration that concerns you is in the last paragraph, 55, because everything else relates to numbers. Paragraph 52 on the last page, this is the paragraph where we changed some text, reservists of RPO it says here were reservists of the army, and then we made a correction saying that they were reservists of the army and police due to which they were included in the units. And then we added that those units were also of police; is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you now confirm that this statement is accurate and do you accept it as your own?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we hereby tender Mr. Vojnovic's statement as 6D1532.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, anything remaining?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. That shall be admitted, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vojnovic, can we now begin with your live testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who told you that you were to become chief of SUP in Prizren and were you given any reasons for that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic told me that I was being sent to Prizren to the post of chief of secretariat because the chief of that particular secretariat was to retire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who signed the decision appointing you and sending you there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The decision sending you there, did it say that you were a member of the MUP staff of the expanded MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: That decision on sending me there did not state that I was a member of the expanded MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did that decision also define your obligations in relation to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: There was nothing in the decision concerning the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your predecessor, when handing the post over to you, did he perhaps say that you were a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I failed to tell you that I was sent there -- actually, the decision said that I was appointed as of the 1st of January; however, I went to Prizren on the 11th of January with Zekavica, who was prior to me chief of secretariat. He retired as of the 31st of December, 1998, the previous year. We went there together and we worked together for two or three days in Prizren. We toured all organizational units, we carried out the hand-over of duty. He did not give me any instructions concerning the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we bring up P1505, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you find that document in your binder, please, P1505.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this decision as part of the hand-over when you became chief of SUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not receive this decision -- in fact, I never received this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see in e-court P1811 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which is the next document in your binder. Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the previous decision was the one on establishing the staff dated 16th of June, 1998, and this decision is the decision on establishment of the staff dated 31st of May, 1999. Were you aware at the time that by way of this decision you were designated as a member of the expanded MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that nor did I ever receive this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now to go back to P1505, the previous document. Do you see here that David Gajic is listed as deputy head of staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were in Kosovo and Metohija, was David Gajic deputy head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I know David Gajic personally. I did not see him in Pristina and I know that he was not head -- deputy head of the staff, naturally, while I was in Prizren, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was replaced by Misa Vilotic in the state security sector, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His full name is Milisav Vilotic, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I know the last name, Vilotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in Kosovo and Metohija in 1999, did you snow that Milisav Vilotic was deputy head of staff of MUP in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was deputy head of the staff from the 1st of January until the 14th of June, 1999, when you left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Mijatovic, a colonel from police administration - and I think towards the end, sometime in May - he was replaced, that is to say he returned to Belgrade and a man with a last name Bozovic, I believe his first name was Dragan, was sent to replace him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here Milorad Lukovic listed as assistant head of staff, that's the fourth name in the list of members. Did you ever know, did you ever learn, directly or indirectly, that Milorad Lukovic, nicknamed Legija, was a member of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know that Miroslav Lukovic was a member of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next name listed is Zivko Trajkovic. While you were in Kosovo, did you ever hear that Zivko Trajkovic was a member of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear that Zivko Trajkovic was a member of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it regulated anywhere, is it prescribed that you as chief of Prizren SUP are responsible for your work to the head of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of such a legal position. As far as I know, that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now bring up P1044.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's in the previous binder, sir. This is a document of the Ministry of the Interior, public security sector, dated 19th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 3 in B/C/S, item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of obligation is set up by way of item 5 in relation to SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: This document of the Ministry of the Interior envisages that SUPs from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, when reporting MUP, need to also report, or rather, send reports to the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In addition to this obligation, is there any other document or regulation setting forth some other obligations for chiefs of SUP or any heads of various professional departments within SUP in relation to the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have a duty to seek any kind of an approval or consent from the MUP staff in order to engage your own units or units that were sent to Prizren SUP in order to carry out tasks in the territory covered by your SUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Practically speaking, there was no need for me to contact staff in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You as head of the Prizren secretariat, in order to do anything, did you have to receive an order from the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have to receive any order from the staff. I mostly organized work and tasks within the competence of MUP based on powers prescribed by law, by legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us take an example. In order to arrest perpetrators of a crime, be they policemen, civilians, or soldiers, did you have to wait for an order from the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have to wait for an order from the staff because these tasks are regulated by legislation, and I simply acted in accordance with the law, that is to say the secretariat in Prizren acted in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about a policeman who comes across a perpetrator who catches somebody committing a crime, does that policeman have to wait for an order?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I have to tell you that that's quite a complex issue. All authorised officials, including policemen, act in accordance with the law. Based on what I know, unfortunately, there are over 200 regulations in force mandating or setting forth some duties concerning policemen in Serbia. So policemen simply acted in accordance with their legal authorities. The Law on Internal Affairs sets forth that a policeman off duty also has to act in accordance with the law in order to carry out his duties. For example, violation of law and order in great extent and so on and similar cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the territory of your SUP there was an antiterrorist activity carried out under the control of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware. As for anti-terrorist activities, we in SUP were in charge of that and PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me now turn to the meetings at the staff in 1999. Would you please turn to D1990 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please read the heading.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "Minutes from the meeting held at the MUP staff in Pristina on 17th of February, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have this exhibit on the screen, please, P1990 -- oh, it's there. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a minutes of a meeting of the MUP staff or of a meeting held at the staff of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of a meeting held at the staff of the MUP, or better yet it is a minutes of a collegium meeting -- a meeting of the minister at the staff of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, would you read the heading, please, where it says: "Minutes" and then what is immediately under that. Just read it aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, staff of the ministry, the 17th of February, 1999, Pristina. "Minutes of a meeting held at the MUP staff in Pristina on the 17th of February, 1999."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's sufficient. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I think that we have discrepancy in English translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It has been dealt with by the witness reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That was the reason for asking him to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read out the first paragraph, what attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by: Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic; public security department chief Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic; chief of the RDB, General Rade Markovic; Assistant Minister Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic; all members of the Pristina MUP staff; Milisav Vilotic, coordinator of the RDB in contacts -- for KiM; all chiefs of SUPs in KiM and SAJ detachment commanders and the state security department centre chiefs in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here "all members of the MUP staff in Pristina." After that we see the name of Milosav Vilotic. What conclusion do you draw from that, that Milosav Vilotic was a member of the MUP staff in Pristina; in that case would his name have been stated here separately?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. It says here all MUP staff members in Pristina, then separately we see Milosav Vilotic as the coordinator for the RDB in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, if a person were to read these minutes and want to know the identities of the members of the Pristina MUP staff, as it says, where would that person go to find the identities of the Pristina MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably I would guess at the head of the staff, he was the best person to know who the members of his staff were. This is my interpretation since I don't see that his deputy is mentioned anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why would you not invite such a person to go and read the decision establishing the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you want to find out the identity of the persons who form any unit of the ministry, whether it be an organizational unit or an ancillary unit, would you not normally go to the decision establishing that body to find out who its members are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not so sure about it since I don't think it was very up-to-date at the time; however, I do agree with you that that would be the best course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further down in the text we see that apart from all of the staff members mentioned we see the chiefs of all SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Reading the document would you say that chiefs of SUPs were members of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In my view and judging by the text, that would not be my conclusion, they would not be members of the Pristina MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It concludes with CRDB chiefs in KiM. The question is the same: When reading this paragraph would you say that state security sector centre chiefs in Kosovo and Metohija were members of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the CRDB in KiM were not members of the staff, at least not according to what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go to page 3 of the document now. It says, and it's easier for me to read than it is for you: "Carefully approach and engage volunteers and conduct that through the reserve forces of the police when we deem that to be necessary." The date in question is the 17th of February, 1999. These words are attributed to Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic. First of all, I'd like to ask you the following: In your area, that is, in the area of Prizren SUP, were there any volunteers with the police forces?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In Prizren SUP there were no volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The minister says: "... when we deem that to be necessary." I realize that I'm asking you to interpret, but what is your interpretation of that phrase when we were preparing ourselves for your testimony, who did you think the minister had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: My conclusion of course was that he meant himself and the leaders from the MUP who attended the meeting at the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There may be another interpretation issue here. Could you please read aloud the sentence to which your attention has been drawn, the one referring to volunteers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Approach with a degree of sensitivity and engage volunteers linking their engagement through the reserve police forces when we deem that to be necessary."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cvetic, who was one of the witnesses of the Prosecution, in his testimony said that Sreten Lukic said that; however, that he uttered those words precisely one month later, which was the 17th of March, 1999. Do you recall or did you attend any meetings at the staff at which you heard Sreten Lukic saying this or something like this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the 17th of March precisely. Concerning the question you put, perhaps it would help for me to see a minutes, if it was a meeting at the MUP staff where chiefs were in attendance, then I might be able to interpret. However, I didn't hear of such a thing, not on the 17th of March, but rather I never heard Sreten Lukic saying anything like it at all or any of the meetings I attended. That is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- well, now it sort of rings a bell. Cvetic was the chief in Kosovska Mitrovica I think. I think he had certain problems. I think he was removed, although I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go to page 1 of the document, please, towards the bottom of the page it says: "The staff planned to carry out, once ordered, three mopping-up operations in the areas of Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica to clear them of terrorists ..." Dragobilje was within your area, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your understanding of this sentence, that the MUP make plans for this action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: My understanding was that we were to do that in the following period. As for Dragobilje, I am certain of it since I had data at my disposal that in that part not only Dragobilje, as we call it nowadays, but there are a number of settlements there. In that area a great many of Siptar terrorists were there, and of course they didn't stay put, they committed crimes. It was my understanding that we who were in charge of that were supposed to plan and take measures, activities, aimed at preventing such terrorist acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move to P1989. It is a meeting with the various police leaders in Kosovo and Metohija. The heading says that, or rather, in the first paragraph it says that the meeting was held with the ministry staff. Please read out the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "On the 4th of April, 1999, beginning at 900 hours, a meeting was held with the chiefs of secretariats in the territory of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija and detachment commanders of the PJP and SAJ as well as JSO with the following agenda."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see from this whether the meeting was attended by any MUP staff members if we read the first and the third paragraph, can we see if there was anyone present from the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: We can see here that only General Sreten Lukic was there on behalf of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this a meeting of the MUP staff then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was a meeting of the chiefs of SUPs in the area of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija, as well as detachment commanders of the PJP, SAJ, and JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was the most senior official at this meeting according to rank and position?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When preparing you for the testimony, we went through the entire document. I wanted to ask you the following. Since the chiefs of SUPs briefed on the situation in their respective areas, can you tell us whether there were some chiefs who did not report on any crime perpetrators apprehended during the previous period. What can we see from these minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To go back to what I said a minute ago, in my assessment this is what contributed to Cvetic being removed from the position of the chief of SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica. Of course there must have been other reasons as well; however, I am not familiar with those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why are you mentioning Cvetic in relation to my previous question when I asked you whether there were any chiefs who had no arrested persons in their territory?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm mentioning him because it was my impression that he was dissatisfied with such a decision. So perhaps that was one more reason for him to act in that way. I am not fully certain, but as far as I remember he was not only removed from office but I think that he also left MUP. I'm not certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I can't put leading questions to you. When this briefing was held, did Ljubinko Cvetic report on the number of the arrested persons in the territory of his secretariat of Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all of us briefed on that, but he had nothing to brief on, nothing to report, because he had none, as far as I know, nothing was recorded and it seemed somewhat irresponsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now turn to page 3. And read the last sentence in this page, the last asterisk.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "Mandatory reporting of chief of secretariats and unit commanders to staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what triggered this request? This is now the 4th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: NATO bombing was already underway. The war was on. It was very difficult to report to the staff, to get in contact with them. Some officers and some heads probably failed to report, so this was a good occasion for us to get in touch to see that we were all alive and fine. I think that in addition to such -- despite such an order, I was not in the position to fully abide by it in Prizren, not because I didn't want to but because very seldom we had the conditions necessary for this. I think, but I'm not fully certain, that at the time the Pristina SUP, the building of the Pristina SUP, had already been bombed. I'm not sure, it was on the 3rd or 4th or 5th, and then following that everything became much more difficult in terms of communications, radio contact and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that they were mandatory dispatches containing orders arriving from the ministry at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In item 2 it says: "Upcoming tasks." By uttering these words, by saying so, what is it that Sreten Lukic is actually doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: He's practically reminding us of our duties, both legal ones and those contained in dispatches of the minister or chief of a sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, fourth asterisk from the bottom, would you please read it on that same page.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "Undertake strict measures in relation to paramilitary units."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this mean to undertake strict or vigorous measures?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: To fully abide by the law and prevent any such phenomenon. However, I have to tell you that the Prizren SUP did not have such problems, at least I had no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did such orders also arrive from the chief of the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we please turn to 6D269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Vojnovic, of where the problems with paramilitary units had arisen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I can't remember just now whether there were any in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, but when paramilitary units were mentioned I know that such problems existed in other parts of the former Yugoslavia. I wouldn't like to burden you with that now, but Bosnia and the like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, during the events in those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, well, please concentrate on my question. I'm anxious to know which areas had a problem with paramilitaries in Kosovo to give rise to this particular provision in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did not have such information and I can confirm that by telling you that I arrived on the 11th of January, 1999, and stayed there until the 14th of June. And as a person in charge of Prizren I can tell you that I did not have such problems. I am more referring to, or rather, I think that this order, "nalog," had a preventive aim, at least that's how I took it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now we're dealing with 6D269 which is a dispatch, signed by chief of public security sector. Would you please turn to page 2, item 7, and read it out to us. Would you be able to read this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "By way of intensified operative work and by undertaking other measures and actions, conduct all necessary checks, record and put under control voluntary units -- paramilitary units and volunteers and their members."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it says here "compile records," what does it actually mean, record or compile records? Who else is recorded?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In the secretariats of the interior, or rather, in the Ministry of the Interior there is an instruction on how records are kept in police stations. And by way of that instruction, the minister specified exactly what records need to be kept and what needs to be recorded, starting from daily chronology and recording thereof to various events. Let me just give you an example of a record. For example, a diary or a log-book of the duty service at the police station, and there are many records of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are perpetrators of crime recorded or listed as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: All events of importance, all persons who were apprehended, as we say in police, and by this I mean perpetrators of crimes, of misdemeanours, people who are listed as wanted, and so on, all of that is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, please turn to 6D238. We need item 5 on page 2. It's difficult to read this and I will read it, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read it. Item 5 reads: "Record or list and put under control volunteers and paramilitary units and their members in order for them to be possibly engaged." What is the meaning of this? Was it intended that they be recorded and engaged or was there another meaning behind this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the leading form of this. I think he could have stopped with his first question without going on and hinting at the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that must be true, Mr. Lukic. Could we not just confine you to the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can even make it shorter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the essence of this text? How do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, this is how I understood this, namely, that in accordance with the instruction we were to keep accurate records of all sorts when it comes to these persons who are reporting to our units voluntarily. To tell you the truth, I did not have such cases and I did not pay any special attention to this provision. Perhaps the author of this provision thought that if, God forbid, such people should appear, we may include them. However, we did not have such cases in the territory of the Prizren SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the first page we can see that this dispatch was sent to all SUPs, 1 through 33. What does this mean? To what territory did this dispatch apply?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that now. This is the dispatch of the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and he sent it to all secretariats, and there were a total of 33 of them in the territory of the entire state.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, P1989, please. Now, these are the minutes from the meeting with senior officials of the police. This is dated 4th of April, 1999. We need page 3. We need sixth asterisk from the bottom or maybe the fifth -- or from the top. It reads: "Ammunition and MES ..." What is MES, please? Would you please read the whole sentence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that MES stands for mines and explosives. "Ammunition and MES to be used rationally and commanders of RPO are to be reminded of that."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the 4th of April, 1999, and commanders of RPOs are mentioned here. What is your interpretation of this sentence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Before giving you a direct answer, I have to say that reserve police squads or RPOs were disbanded sometime in mid-March just before the war began. And what we explained in the statement that was given was meant to say that members of these reserve police squads or RPOs were mostly mobilised. Some of them joined the Army of Yugoslavia because that was their wartime assignment and some of them went to MUP because this is where they had again wartime assignments in reserve forces. Most likely this here implied that a small number of members of RPOs remained because I'm not sure that all of them were mobilised for a number of reasons, one of the reasons being that perhaps they were not fit for military service, they were not considered as potential conscripts, and the other reason being that it was difficult to do all that under the circumstances at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you now please go to the following page of that document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you do, let's try to be rational about this, Mr. Vojnovic. You say that the reservists -- sorry, the reserve police units had been disbanded by this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Reserve police detachments I think that we use in this trial for this formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we used -- units was being used yesterday. We know what it means. You say that these reserve police groupings were disbanded in March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the question is: Why in April is Mr. Lukic telling the RPO commanders or asking for them to be told that ammunition and mines and explosives have to be used very rationally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I've said, most likely General Lukic thought or had information that not all members of RPOs had been mobilised. As regards the use of ammunition and mines and explosives, it was our position at the secretariats and with the leadership of the MUP to use those rationally. At the beginning of the war there were some people wearing uniforms, although they were not supposed to. They had their own reasons, maybe they liked it. As the chief of SUP, I was ordered not to wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've lost me now. What has the wearing of a uniform got to do with the rational use of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the same meeting I think uniforms were discussed, or rather, the wearing of uniforms by people who had no right to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's concentrate on the ammunition and the mines and the explosives. Either the RPOs were disbanded or they weren't; now, which is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The truth is that they had been disbanded by way of mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you just don't understand this instruction at all; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to explain and to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't want you to speculate. We want you to tell us what you know as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no information whether they had any mines or explosives; however, I do know that they had infantry weapons as well as combat kits of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when you say "they," you're referring to people who had not been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean all members of RPOs when they were being established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you go to the last, fourth, page of this document? The seventh bullet from the top, command and control. Please read it out loud and tell us what it means. This is attributed to Obrad Stevanovic, assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In this sentence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "Control and command of units in the area of a secretariat is done by the chiefs. In the area of the secretariat we had the reserve police forces within the secretariat" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- "the police forces, regular police forces, as well as the PJP within the secretariat in Prizren and sent units. These are the units he had in mind when conducting regular tasks and assignments. Those assignments were within the purview of the MUP and they came by way of daily assignments of the secretariat."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to be clear about this, did he have in mind the engagement of units in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. That calls for speculation on the part of this witness. How can he know what the minister had in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us go to P1996, please. It is the 7th of May, 1999. In the heading we have the ministry staff. Please read out the title.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "Minutes of a meeting held at the MUP staff of Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina on the 7th of May, 1999, which began at 1100 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see on the front page how many people from the staff attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it was only General Lukic -- no, sorry. Under number 1, assistant MUP staff head, Colonel Stevanovic [as interpreted]; and Blagojevic Tomislav as well as Pesic Blagoje, assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read out --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 26, line 12, it says Colonel Stevanovic, should be Colonel Mijatovic. It would cause a great confusion if we leave it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read out paragraph 2 as well as 3, in the course of work, as well as items 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: "In the course of the meeting MUP generals, the MUP of Serbia, that is, participated. Lieutenant-Colonel Stevanovic, Obrad, who's assistant minister; and under 2, chief of the MUP UKP Major-General Dragan Ilic, with his associates: Chief of the KTC, Vladimir Aleksic and head of the department in the UKP Sinisa Spanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what KTC means.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Crime forensic centre, which fell under the -- under the MUP. It was one of the organizational units of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 7 of the document, please. General Dragan Ilic is recorded there as taking part -- excuse me, it is page 8. In preparing you for the testimony we read what General Ilic had said. Do you recall from that time, and what was your understanding of General Dragan Ilic's stay in Kosovo and Metohija with his associates around the 7th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: General Ilic was the chief of the crime police administration at the seat of the ministry. He is the leader of one of the most important or maybe the most important professional areas dealing with crime. I believe before this meeting with us he had another meeting with heads of crime police departments at the seat of the secretariat as territorial MUP units, whereby they discussed problems that had to do with crime and other issues they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In one of the items he says: "In order to clear the terrain a plan had been devised distributed to all secretariats and crime police departments defining tasks." Who created that plan in your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In my understanding the plan of sanitization was made by the administration in charge of crime police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In page 6 you are mentioned as taking part in the discussion in item 5. Item 5, the sixth bullet from the top, you say: "61 persons were taken before competent courts; however, disproportionate sentences have been handed down. Out of ten judgements, nine were probation and one person was acquitted." I wanted to ask you this: Why did you discuss this issue at that very meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I raised this issue because I had occasion to mention that problem in front of the most important person in the domain of fighting crime. Of course I wished that there were less such cases and I was hoping that in cooperation with the Ministry of Justice he would deal or at least reduce the number of such occurrences.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document go to page 9, please. We need the first bullet on page 9. Here it says that Sreten Lukic said: "The number of 27 crimes of murder seems small, since there is information that there were more on-site investigations that had been carried out and that there were more criminal reports that had been submitted for those crimes."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was your understanding of these words uttered by Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: My understanding was that he wanted to remind us of our obligation to keep orderly files and registers. It seems that the registers on the number of crimes did not tally, or rather, were not up-to-date in terms of the number of crimes and the number of on-site investigations and criminal reports submitted to the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Two bullets down it says: "In cases of arson and murder, do not wait; the suspects must be handed over immediately to the competent judge with a criminal report and you must ask for a sentence to be pronounced immediately. These sorts of problems have still not been cleared up, especially in Kosovo Polje and Podujevo, as well as Prizren and Djakovica, while Gnjilane seems to have resolved certain problems." What was the thrust of this part of Sreten Lukic's presentation? What was your understanding of it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In my understanding, in a way he wanted to draw our attention to how we should conduct our work. In his presentation he cited the good example of Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 10, please, paragraph 3 -- I believe we'll have to resume after the break. It is time I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this your last reference to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just finish with this document and then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 3, the second bullet point, these should be the words of Sreten Lukic, who says: "I mention in particular that in the work of OPG, the chief of SUP gives permission for certain actions and informs the head of staff." What was your understanding of Sreten Lukic's words?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, members of the OPG were regular forces of the secretariat and of the PJP. It was about a dozen or ten policemen who were trained to carry out the more difficult tasks and assignments, and in my assessment and understanding, General Lukic was concerned about the fate of those people. He didn't want to see any harm come to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the staff command and use OPGs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Vojnovic, we have to have a break at this stage, that will be for 20 minutes; while we have that break, could you leave the courtroom, please, with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Judge Nosworthy is again unwell, and we will continue in her absence. Later in the final session Judge Chowhan will not be with us because of urgent personal reasons, again we will continue. We consider it to be in the interests of justice that we continue in the absence of the two Judges, who will have a chance to read the transcript and will miss hopefully only a short part of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I said that the last item I was going to ask you from document P1996, but that was the last one and now I'm going to ask you something else. In the next bullet it says: "Establish urgently control of police wearing uniforms. Uniforms may only be worn by members of the police with a P status and the reserve police when they are engaged." What does this P status mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Uniformed policemen or police, short.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you as members of SUP fall into that category?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Green uniform is worn only in anti-terrorist actions. All other members who are not entitled to wear uniform, they need to return their uniforms in order to work in civilian clothes starting from chief of SUP down to the lowest rank of employees." Were there policemen who wore a blue camouflage uniform in combat activities in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something about anti-terrorist activities before the war. In the territory of your SUP we used to refer to these actions as anti-terrorist actions before the war and you corrected me by saying that those were anti-terrorist activities. Tell me, please, why do you think that it's more accurate to say "anti-terrorist activity"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In the police sense of the word, when it comes to terrorists, they are considered as perpetrators of crimes because these are citizens, nationals, of the Republic of Serbia. And in that sense the police has an obligation to prevent commission of such crimes through a number of measures or through a number of activities. For example, by detecting, apprehending, detaining, taking in to see competent authorities, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in the territory of your SUP were any anti-terrorist activities carried out before the beginning of bombing; and if so, which?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Practically speaking, in 1999 when I arrived, as far as I remember, sometime in March we had a number of anti-terrorist activities. As the beginning of bombing approached we used to call it the D-Day, the security situation became more complex, especially in the areas that were of interest due to security reasons, such as populated areas between Prizren municipality and those of Orahovac and Suva Reka. And then in the villages above Prizren travelling towards Brezovica mount, such as Jeskovo, Kabas, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did members of the Army of Yugoslavia and PJP sometimes stop by your office?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was planning and coordination carried out in your office between the commander of 549th Brigade of the Army of Yugoslavia and commander of the 37th Detachment of PJP and commander of your company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Going back slightly, were members of the PJP from your area trained in the provisions of international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to the curriculum for training of PJP I truly can't say anything because I wasn't involved in it. While I was in the Prizren secretariat, I don't have any information about them being trained; however, if this is not too extensive I can tell you that I personally completed a seminar in the International Red Cross Committee in Serbia on the topic of humanitarian law and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what sort of circumstances were envisaged in which you would need to apply international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly state of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, the reference is to NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the only reason you're aware of for training in international humanitarian law is for the engagement with NATO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if you understood me well. International Committee of Red Cross, in agreement with the Ministry of the Interior, organized a seminar on the topic with a number of senior officials from MUP secretariat and teachers teaching at police schools.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what I want to be clear on is that had nothing to do with your treatment of Albanian terrorists; it was to do with potential treatment of NATO protagonists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time when I attended training, it wasn't related or I didn't understand it to be related either to members of the Albanian minority or members of NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does police use laws of war in its work or laws in force in its state?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the existing regulations, police carries out regular duties and tasks from the competence of MUP. Regular duties and tasks from the competence of MUP are regulated by the current legislation of the state, legislation and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We spoke about actions carried out in your jurisdiction before the war. Did you ever see a plan for engaging police units, for example, the 37th Detachment and your company, in the two actions that you mentioned, in Jeskovo and Kabas?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in drafting of the plan?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you inform anyone about these two actions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I was duty-bound, in accordance with the instruction on mandatory information, to inform the MUP and the MUP staff on a 24-hour basis and I did so. I think that at the time when there was activity aimed at preventing terrorist action in Jeskovo and Kabas, we also had a mission of observers there; and we invariably informed them of all complex activities related to anti-terrorist activities regularly and it was mostly myself who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether representatives of KVM had any complaints about how these two actions were carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to communicate with the representative of the mission of observers, there were no complaints. I can tell you that we carried out an on-site investigation together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether during that on-site investigation, whether there were any dead bodies found of people who were killed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to Jeskovo, I think that we had information to the effect that there was a camp, an Albanian camp, where they trained Albanian terrorists. And one of the reasons for organizing that activity was to detain members of that anti-terrorist group. Naturally, that was not the only reason for organizing it. We also had information to the effect that they moved out residents of several Albanian villages. There were people who were killed, and I couldn't really give you a number. It was recorded, people were prosecuted, and you can verify this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was anybody's approval required in order for MUP units to be used? I'm referring to PJP detachment and your company.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When PJP detachments were sent to Kosovo and Metohija, was their role known in advance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, their role was known, and practically by mere fact that they were recruited or mobilised, their task was made clear to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was their task?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my understanding, they had several tasks. One of them was to carry out regular duties and tasks in the territory of the MUP where they were sent together with other people working in that MUP in accordance with the daily schedule of work. In case of some large-scale activities or where the entire establishment group was sent, they carried out various tasks aimed at prevention of terrorist acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there any need to issue some special sorts of order to engage PJP units prior to each individual action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no need to do that; however, the PJP company of the Prizren SUP needed to get in touch with its command, which was I think located in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about this command located in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: That's the intervention brigade of PJP in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the number of the brigade? If you don't know, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was 127th or 124th, but I'm not sure, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see any special map relating to one of these two activities which only had the tasks of the police marked on it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Before the activities were carried out, I would receive a map normally from the commander of the PJP company from Prizren or from the commander of the PJP detachment, Colonel Mitrovic. However, what this map meant for me was that I could potentially assist my company and naturally others if needed. So I didn't see that map as some sort of a combat map because I wasn't qualified for that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a map did you receive, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: It was on A4 format, hard copy, grey colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does it have a name, that sort of a map that you would normally receive?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Right now it escapes me, truly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I clarify the distinction with what you dealt with earlier. You were earlier asked if you ever saw a plan for engaging police units, for example, the 37th Detachment and your company in the two actions that you mentioned in Jeskovo and Kabas, and you did that you did not see such a plan. Are we now talking about a different type of plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that I saw no plan, I was referring to written plans, because together with the map I received nothing else. I would receive just a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I asked you, about the name of the map and what it had marked on it, were there any circles or what was there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember right now. This map was, or rather, there were some marks marking certain locations. If I can explain, I can explain how I understood it, but I can't remember the exact name of the map. For example, if I was told that in a certain location there was a wounded person, then it was easy for me to send assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the map coded?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was the coded map. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see P2015 in e-court now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have 2015 in your binder?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see the order at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that as of the 25th of March, 1999, there was an action carried out in the area of Orahovac and Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There were anti-terrorist activities, were there not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who notified you of that action, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. They didn't need to inform me, since almost daily General Delic, myself, the commander of the 37th Detachment saw each other and we spent time together. There were no secrets among us, at least I think. Daily we talked, discussing this and other topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who made the plan of this action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I do now, since it is mentioned here; however, I had no occasion to see that before and I wasn't informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the coordination between Commander Delic and MUP officials who participated in the planning of this action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to grasp the concept of coordination. If I was there, they would never excuse themselves. They didn't hide any of their conversations from me; however, I did not participate in the creation of this plan. I didn't decide on when activities were to be undertaken. And as the head of secretariat I wasn't present in the territory where these units carried out those activities at that time of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P1981, please. We see this order of the 549th Motorised Brigade dated the 23rd of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see it on the screen in front of you, if you can follow.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember concerning this action whether coordination was planned and carried out in your presence, in your office?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, it wasn't carried out in my office. Mostly we met in the barracks, within the perimeter of the barracks in Prizren at the PJP commander's office, Mr. Mitrovic. It would usually take place in the afternoon. We were on such good terms that, practically speaking, we didn't hold formal meetings, strictly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you discuss when you were together?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Of course we discussed the activities of members of the Siptar terrorist forces. We also discussed, of course, our duties and obligations concerning the carrying out of joint patrols, joint check-points. We discussed those taken into custody and other things. I cannot recall all of them. We discussed problems in units, the obligations of the secretariat in terms of logistics, its obligations concerning conscripts who failed to respond to draft calls and similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on this document of the 549th Brigade we can see that your PJP company participated as well. I want to ask you again what sort of uniform was worn by the members of your PJP company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Green uniforms -- excuse me, excuse me, blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Members of your company green or camouflage green, members of your PJP company when going into combat?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: They wore blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In combat activities in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. I need some time to focus. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said green. I just wanted you to tell me what sort of green.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage green. You confused me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you keep going? You told me that you tire easily, but can we keep going?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the last answer was blue, but he did say green somewhere along the way just in case there's any doubt in your mind over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just need the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He already said before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Members of your PJP company or PJP detachment, did they wear black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the town of Prizren as well as other towns in your area, did you have joint patrols with the VJ or joint check-points?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Both, patrols and check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you had joint check-points, for example, in the territory of your SUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Along the main roads to Zur going from Prizren, that is, towards the Albanian border, then in the outskirts of Prizren and in the village of Zur which is some 7 or 8 kilometres away; then towards Dusanovo, which is an outskirts of Prizren towards Orahovac and Djakovica. Then on the same road at the location called Zrze; next in the outskirts of Orahovac entering and leaving Orahovac, that is; then at the entrance and exit point of Suva Reka going from Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what military units were there in your area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I find the terminology difficult. I hope you won't hold it against me, but there were members of the VJ from the garrison or barracks in Prizren. The 500 and something, I forgot the number, I didn't even try to memorise it. Then there were members of the army who came from Serbia proper, Kraljevo, Krusevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any army members in the town of Prizren itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: There was both police and army in the town of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see any units of the Ministry of Defence, such as civilian protection units in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning disciplinary measures, can you tell us whether you held any positions which had to do with disciplinary responsibility of policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I worked at the disciplinary court of the MUP of Serbia, the first -- the basic and the first-instance court, as well as the next level up. Of course that was not my permanent position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What sort of positions did you hold?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I was the prosecutor, a member of the chamber, and the president of the court, and I worked in the first-instance court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the relationship is between the disciplinary misdemeanour and criminal proceedings, do they overlap? Are they exclusive of each other?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: These or such proceedings are independent and separate, although they can take place simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to go through certain counts of indictment -- of the indictment with you, such as Count 72 of the indictment speaks of deportation. Did you know that on the 25th of March of 1999 or were you informed that the forces of the FRY surrounded the town of Suva Reka and that many houses were set on fire, the police drove women, the elderly, and children away, and that a number of forces from Serbia killed a number of males found there? Did you know that at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not receive such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 31st of March, 1999, that some 80.000 Kosovar Albanians gathered in the municipality of Suva Reka, that they hailed from that municipality and they gathered at Belanica and that the next day the forces of Serbia and Yugoslavia shelled the village, forcing the displaced persons to flee?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have such information at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever been informed concerning item 75 of the count of murder, 75(b), that in the morning hours of the 24th of March, 1999, the forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded a part or a territory around the Berisha family housing compound, whereby at least 44 civilians were killed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I had no such information at my disposal. Concerning the event ... I learned of that event when Colonel Mitrovic was arrested. I also heard further details of the case concerning -- before the special court in Belgrade for war crimes, where I appeared as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning Bela Crkva, item 75(b), the 25th of March, 1999, or around that date, the forces of FRY and Serbia surrounded and attacked the village of Bela Crkva. It is alleged that they killed at least 12 persons and that they opened fire later killing some 65 Kosovar Albanians. Did you know that at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have that information at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you at the time know that, as alleged in the indictment under (c) that in Mala Krusa on the 25th of March, 1999, the village of Mala Krusa was attacked and around 105 Kosovar Albanians were killed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning item 72(a), did you know that in the morning of the 25th of March, 1999, the forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded the village of Celina by using tanks and armoured vehicles and shelled the village, they expelled the population from Celina?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that on that same day, on the 25th of March, the people were deported from the village of Pirane?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that on the 28th of March, 1999, the police went house to house in Prizren, forcing people to leave the town of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the war and immediately before the war in 1999, were houses burned in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: While I was in Prizren just one house burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did NATO shell Prizren, the town itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that there are records of that. I don't know exactly how many times a day they did it, but they definitely did it every day. They shelled populated areas, facilities, civilians, and naturally police and the army, that goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we did your proofing, is it true that you had some trouble remembering people and places, their names, because you stayed in Kosovo for a very brief period of time and we were unable to talk about specific details and specific crimes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. I spent a very brief period of time there under very difficult circumstances, and also by nature I'm such that I unintentionally forget certain things, figures, names, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: After the withdrawal of Serb forces, were houses in Prizren set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: I have to tell you, after they relocated, I think that the entire Serbian settlement was on fire, I think that settlement was called Podkaljaja. I think as we were moving out it was on fire, and subsequently I heard that it had burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that a part of the town of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's almost in the centre of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I have for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Vojnovic, I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'd like for you to turn to document P1989.

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: It just happens to be open right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Fine. Did you attend this meeting held as you can see on that particular date?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As you can see, was Sainovic present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS VOJNOVIC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you look at the introductory part you can see that he's not mentioned in the list of attendees in the very beginning; however, if you turn to page 4 of your document --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
